correctness.rationale: For the precise independent p-tremble model, each of two other ballots independently remains fixed with probability 1-p or goes to either other candidate with probability p/2. Independently enumerating all nine terminal opponent profiles with exact rational polynomial weights gives, for top-minus-middle actions at truthful (A,B,C), constant (1-2rho_i)/3; at unanimous (A,A,A), zero constant and linear coefficients (5-4rho1)/3 for voter 1 and (4-5rho_i)/3 for voters 2,3. Signs are strict on 0<rho1<1/2, 1/2<rho2,rho3<4/5. Worst ballot is strictly dominated for any p>0 by favorite, since each pivotal opponent tally has positive probability; thus only the compared actions matter. These are exact leading coefficients, so a common sufficiently small p exists per parameter triple, proving the 2-cycle of full ballots and distinct polls. For one or two voters and any m, conditioning on the other voter gives strict favorite dominance; for any N and two candidates, favorite weakly dominates pointwise and is strictly better on a positive-probability pivotal tally. Those arguments prove simultaneous minimality, not merely numerics. Independent checker confirms the six polynomial profiles at rho=(1/4,3/4,3/4). No assertion for a fixed tremble p uniformly over the full open parameter box.
